status: Draft for implementation within P4/P5; not shipped, not radio-tested and not a lost-owner recovery bypass.

pending_research: Check all boot/install identity anchors before permitting TokenSHA256 replacement.
Check desktop credential namespace/setup lease and saved-attempt coordination before adding pending slots.

invariants: Managed signout and tailnet rejoin continue to preserve the existing local owner.
Rotation is an explicit separately authenticated known-owner operation; no trust-on-first-use reset or privilege bootstrap.
Client generates and durably saves the candidate credential before sending any mutation. Server never generates an irreplaceable secret reply.
One bounded pending proposal per installation; preserve old owner until candidate commit proves possession.
Authenticated old-owner prepare binds installationID, proposalID and new hash; identical retries are idempotent, conflicting proposals refused.
Candidate credential authorizes only commit of that prepared proposal until commit; it is not ordinary admin authority beforehand.
Commit atomically persists the new hash, clears pending proposal and retires active PD session/arms; never keys/restarts/rearms.
Lost prepare/commit replies and app crash recover using already-saved keys and exact installation/proposal identity; old-key ordinary authority revoked after commit.
Uncertain native persistence fails closed, retains both client credentials and never asserts the old key is still valid.
No host-root authority, arbitrary target/path/command operation or new privilege entry.
No pending-candidate expiry based on unqualified radio wall clock; explicit exact-proposal cancellation by authenticated old owner.
Preserve tailnet identity/hostname/routes/sharing; rotation affects only local owner credential and PD session authority.
required_tests: No owner/foreign owner/legacy mode/installation mismatch rejection
Conflicting and duplicate proposals, old/new key admission before/after commit
Lost prepare reply, lost commit reply, client deletion/session replacement/credential-write timeout
Pre-rename failure vs post-rename persistence uncertainty; process restart from each durable state
Failed prepare/commit save preserves or fails-closed prior session as appropriate
Active receive-only session retires on successful commit, no automatic Start/arm/TX
Only after build/package verification: ordinary owner UI known-owner rotation, receipt-loss recovery and exact resource audit on8600
